**Financial Highlights**


- **Net revenue increased 7.3% compared to Q3 2025, driven primarily by growth in the Wholesale and Direct-to-Consumer ("DTC") channels.**
- **Wholesale revenue increased 8.1%, while DTC revenue increased 8.5%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of year-over-year DTC growth.**
- **Packaged coffee distribution increased 4.6 percentage points to 58.7% on an All Commodity Volume ("ACV") weighted basis.**
- **Net loss was $8.7 million in Q3 2026, compared to a net loss of $1.2 million in Q3 2025, while Adjusted EBITDA increased 12.3% to $9.5 million from $8.4 million in the prior year.**
- **Reaffirmed full-year 2026 outlook of at least 8% revenue growth and at least 35% Adjusted EBITDA growth, incorporating approximately $3 million in expected fourth-quarter revenue headwinds from the divestiture of a non-core DTC brand and planned Outpost closures.**


SALT LAKE CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- **BRC Inc.** (NYSE: BRCC, the "Company" or "Black Rifle"), a Veteran-founded, mission-driven premium coffee company, today announced financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026.


“A key priority during the third quarter was making Black Rifle Coffee more accessible to consumers and creating more opportunities for them to engage with our brand,” said BRCC Chief Executive Officer Chris Mondzelewski. “We expanded distribution through new retail partners and increased our presence within existing accounts. Our campaign celebrating America’s 250th birthday helped broaden awareness and encourage trial among new consumers. Wholesale delivered another quarter of growth, while Direct-to-Consumer recorded its fourth consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth. We also launched Project Core, our multi-year initiative to sharpen our focus on our core coffee business and brand, improve profitability and earnings quality, simplify our operations, and reduce the capital intensity of our business. Our goal is to build on the growth we’re seeing while capturing more of the value that growth creates.”


“Third-quarter gross profit and Adjusted EBITDA increased, benefiting in part from refunds of previously paid tariffs,” said BRCC Chief Financial Officer Matt Amigh. “We also made meaningful progress on Project Core. We signed a definitive agreement to sell our Manchester roasting facility to a longstanding manufacturing partner, securing a long-term production relationship while we continue to develop our proprietary roasts. We initiated plans to close 12 company-operated Outposts, modified eight leases for locations we no longer intend to develop, and completed the divestiture of a non-core DTC brand. These actions mark a significant step toward a more asset-light operating model, which we expect will support franchise-led retail growth, lower capital requirements, and create a more efficient cost structure. We are reaffirming our full-year 2026 outlook of at least 8% revenue growth and at least 35% Adjusted EBITDA growth, even after incorporating the expected revenue impact of the brand divestiture and Outpost closures.”

**Third Quarter 2026 Results**


Net revenue for the third quarter of 2026 increased 7.3% to $108.0 million, compared to $100.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. Wholesale revenue increased 8.1% to $72.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $67.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Growth in the Wholesale channel was primarily driven by expanded distribution of packaged coffee, including entry into the dollar channel, continued gains in grocery, and pricing.


Direct-to-Consumer ("DTC") revenue increased 8.5% to $30.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $27.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by growth through third-party digital retail marketplaces, partially offset by lower subscription revenue and the divestiture of a non-core brand during the quarter. Revenue from Black Rifle Coffee shops ("Outposts") decreased 8.0% to $5.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $5.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decline reflected lower sales at Company-operated Outposts, partially offset by growth in franchise and non-traditional locations.


Gross profit increased 8.0% to $40.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $37.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. Gross margin increased 25 basis points to 37.1% in the third quarter of 2026, from 36.9% in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in gross margin was primarily driven by pricing actions, approximately $3.5 million in refunds of previously paid tariffs, and productivity improvements. These benefits were partially offset by higher green coffee costs, increased trade spending, higher third-party marketplace fees associated with e-commerce sales growth, and increased transportation costs.


Marketing expenses increased 18.1% to $10.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $8.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. As a percentage of revenue, marketing expenses increased 90 basis points to 9.5% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 8.6% in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher spending on content production and media, influencer programs, agency support and ad placement, partially offset by lower shopper marketing and event costs.


Salaries, wages and benefits expenses increased 7.5% to $15.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $14.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase reflects higher stock-based compensation, employee benefit costs and base salaries, partially offset by lower severance expense. As a percentage of revenue, salaries, wages and benefits expenses remained flat at 14.3% in both periods.


General and administrative ("G&A") expenses decreased 2.7% to $12.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $12.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. As a percentage of revenue, G&A expenses decreased 120 basis points to 11.7% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 12.9% in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by lower depreciation and amortization expense, outside services, software costs and legal fees, partially offset by costs associated with the termination of Outpost leases in connection with Project Core.


Other operating expenses, net increased to $9.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. As a percentage of revenue, other operating expenses increased 800 basis points to 8.6% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 0.6% in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the impairment of certain Outpost locations during 2026 as a result of the initiation of Project Core, as well as a legal contingency accrual, partially offset by gains on lease terminations and the divestiture of a non-core brand.


Net loss for the third quarter of 2026 was $8.7 million, and Adjusted EBITDA was $9.5 million, compared to a net loss of $1.2 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $8.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.


**Financial Outlook**


The Company is reaffirming its full-year 2026 guidance based on current market conditions, including commodity costs and planned growth investments. Management remains focused on consistent execution to drive revenue growth, margin improvement, Adjusted EBITDA expansion and stronger cash generation. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure.

**About BRC Inc.**


Black Rifle Coffee Company (BRCC) is a Veteran-founded premium coffee company and lifestyle brand serving beverages to people who love America. Founded in 2014 by Green Beret Evan Hafer, Black Rifle develops their explosive roast profiles with the same mission focus they learned while serving in the military. BRCC is committed to supporting Veterans, active-duty military, first responders and the American way of life.


To learn more, visit[www.blackriflecoffee.com](http://www.blackriflecoffee.com/) , subscribe to the BRCC newsletter, or follow along on social media.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


In addition to financial measures prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States ("GAAP"), this press release contains, and the conference call will contain, non-GAAP financial measures, including EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Gross Profit, Adjusted Operating Expenses, DTC revenue, excluding divested brand, Free Cash Flow and Net Leverage Ratio. We rely on both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate the performance of our business. The non-GAAP financial measures, as defined below, are not defined or calculated under principles, standards or rules that comprise GAAP. Accordingly, the non-GAAP financial measures we use and refer to in this press release and/or the conference call should not be viewed as a substitute for performance measures derived in accordance with GAAP. Our definitions of EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Gross Profit, Adjusted Operating Expenses, DTC revenue, excluding divested brand, Free Cash Flow and Net Leverage Ratio described below are specific to our business and you should not assume that they are comparable to similarly titled financial measures of other companies.


We define EBITDA as net income (loss) before interest, tax expense, depreciation and amortization expense. We define Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA adjusted for equity-based compensation, lease termination and modification costs, net, loss on impairment of assets, loss on disposal of assets, non-routine legal expenses, transactions expenses and restructuring fees and related costs. For the third and fourth quarters of 2025, Adjusted EBITDA also reflects adjustments for the gain on the sale of property, losses on impairment of certain assets, transactions expenses and contract termination costs, none of which occurred in the first six months of 2026 or 2025. We define Adjusted Gross Profit as gross profit adjusted for depreciation and amortization and restructuring fees and related costs. We define Adjusted Operating Expenses as Operating Expenses adjusted for depreciation and amortization, equity-based compensation, lease termination and modification costs, net, non-routine legal expenses and restructuring fees and related costs. We define DTC revenue, excluding divested brand, as DTC revenue adjusted for divested brand DTC revenue. We define Free Cash Flow as net cash provided by (used in) operating activities adjusted for purchases of property, plant and equipment. We define Net Leverage Ratio as total principal amounts of debt less cash and cash equivalents, divided by Adjusted EBITDA.


When used in conjunction with GAAP financial measures, we believe that EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Gross Profit, Adjusted Operating Expenses, DTC revenue, excluding divested brand, Free Cash Flow and Net Leverage Ratio are useful supplemental measures of operating performance and liquidity because these measures facilitate comparisons of historical performance by excluding non-cash items such as equity-based compensation and other amounts not directly attributable to our primary operations, such as lease termination and modification costs, net, non-routine legal expenses and restructuring fees and related costs. Adjusted EBITDA is also a key metric used internally by our management to evaluate performance and develop internal budgets and forecasts. Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as an analytical tool and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for analyzing our results as reported under GAAP and may not provide a complete understanding of our operating results as a whole. Some of these limitations are (i) they do not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, our working capital needs, (ii) they do not reflect our interest expense or the cash requirements necessary to service interest or principal payments on our debt, (iii) they do not reflect our tax expense or the cash requirements to pay our taxes, (iv) they do not reflect historical capital expenditures or future requirements for capital expenditures or contractual commitments, (v) although equity-based compensation expenses are non-cash charges, we rely on equity compensation to compensate and incentivize employees, directors and certain consultants, and we may continue to do so in the future and (vi) although depreciation, amortization and impairments are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized will often have to be replaced in the future, and these non-GAAP measures do not reflect any cash requirements for such replacements.
